newsitem.title: UK: Mark/lira up, other crosses steady in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Mark/lira up, other crosses steady in quiet trade.

text.p: The mark firmed on the lira by late European afternoon trade, but was drifting against other European currencies amid an absence of new factors.
Traders cited weakness in Italian government bonds and worries about Italy's budget timetable as reasons behind mark/lira's firmness in an otherwise quiet market.

"There's nothing really new coming out, but there is some doubt about how Italy can form its budget for 1998 earlier than planned. That's seen by the market as a sign of difficulty in Italy's joining EMU in the first round," said one trader at an Italian bank in London.

Italy's government has floated the idea of bringing forward the 1998 budget by several months to show its determination to clean up public finances and boost confidence in its credentials to join EMU. However, government politicians said on Wednesday that the plan was still under review.
The mark was at 984.20/45 lire at 1611 GMT, up from its late Wednesday level of 979.20/50.
The mark crosses showed scant reaction to decisions by the Bank of France and Swiss National Bank to keep key interest rates on hold after their regular policy meetings today.
The BOF kept its intervention rate and emergency lending rate at 3.10 and 4.60 percent respectively, while the SNB left its discount rate unchanged at 1.00 percent.
The mark was at 3.3760/63 French francs against Wednesday's 3.3751/56, while mark/Swiss was at 86.10/12 against 85.97/99.
